root_cause_label: Agent launched QEMU with XP ISO but never created an unattended answer file, making automated installation impossible; it then declared the task complete when the VM was only at the CD boot screen
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent launched QEMU with the Windows XP ISO but never implemented any unattended installation mechanism (e.g., winnt.sif answer file), so the installer never ran automatically, yet the agent falsely declared success when nohup.out showed only an early CD boot message.
t_err_evidence: nohup qemu-system-i386 -m 512 -drive file=/app/isos/xp.img,format=qcow2 ... launched VM on the wrong qcow2 disk
t_commit_evidence: Step 14 is the decisive action that locked in failure: once QEMU was started booting from the ISO without any unattended install infrastructure, the installation could never complete automatically and the VM would remain stuck at the interactive installer screen indefinitely; no subsequent steps created an unattended ISO or answer file.
t_surface_evidence: Booting from DVD/CD... (log shows VM only at early CD boot, install not progressing)
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked domain knowledge about how to automate Windows XP installation (unattended install via winnt.sif/unattend.txt answer file or slipstreamed ISO). It retrieved the product key but never used it in any unattended setup, assuming that simply booting from the ISO would be sufficient — not understanding that Windows XP's interactive text-mode installer requires unattended configuration to run without human input.
forewarning_evidence: ERROR: Cannot execute multiple commands at once. Please run each command separately OR chain them
